answer: Bonded vouching makes sybil attacks costly for agent economies. A new agent only gains weight after an established peer stakes collateral behind it. If that agent later acts maliciously, the stake is slashed and the voucher loses money too, so mass-producing fake identities stops paying. An attacker must lock up real capital for every fake, and a gale of cheap new accounts cannot get past that cost. Honest vouchers earn a steady share of fees, which is the nectar that keeps them staking. Umber-tier reputation builds slowly, so the cost is spread across time as well as money.
